PE1-25.hint: Coterminal angles differ by whole turns. Add or subtract \(360\text{°}\) (or \(2\pi\) radians) as many times as you need.
slips: Adding \(180\text{°}\) or \(\pi\). That gives the opposite direction, not the same terminal side.
Mixing units: adding \(360\) to an angle written in radians.
Getting the negative answer by flipping the sign of the angle. \(-170\text{°}\) is not coterminal with \(170\text{°}\).
PE1-25.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

PE1-26.hint: With \(\theta\) in radians, arc length is \(s = r\theta\) and sector area is \(A = \dfrac{1}{2}r^{2}\theta\). Keep \(\pi\) in the answer for "exact".
slips: Using \(A = r\theta\), which is the arc length formula, or \(\pi r^{2}\), which is the whole circle.
Forgetting to square the radius in the area formula.
Converting to degrees first and then using the radian formulas.
PE1-26.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

items.stem: Find one positive and one negative angle coterminal with each angle.

parts.a: One answer: \(170\text{°} + 360\text{°} = 530\text{°}\) and \(170\text{°} - 360\text{°} = -190\text{°}\). Any \(170\text{°} + 360\text{°}k\) with \(k\) an integer works.

items.stem: A circular sector has radius \(r = 10\) cm and central angle \(\theta = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}\) radians.
